intro: Here's the premise: telegram bot api send message should cost nothing to get started. Between open-source projects, free API tiers and self-hostable tools, it can. Below is the working setup we actually use, plus the gotchas we hit.

We'll walk through Telegram Bot API, Mastodon API, Bluesky At Protocol, and Keep a changelog — and finish with the questions people actually ask, so you can check before you buy anything. You shouldn't have to buy anything.

sections.heading: Telegram Bot API
paragraphs: The foundation looks like this: The Telegram Bot API is free, HTTP-based and needs nothing but a token from @BotFather.

Which, in day-to-day terms, means: Create a bot in one message, then send and receive messages, create channels, and drive webhooks entirely over plain HTTPS. It is the cheapest 'social media' channel a self-publishing site can own, and this blog posts to it when a token is configured.
The links in the sources section go straight to the primary docs.
bullets: Message @BotFather and /newbot to get a token
Optionally set a webhook with setWebhook for incoming events

sections.heading: Mastodon API
paragraphs: First, the thing that actually matters: Mastodon's API is free and fully documented — any instance lets you register an app and post programmatically.

Concretely: Create an app in your instance's developer settings, exchange it for a token, and the REST API handles statuses, follows and search. Because the whole platform is open source and federated, posting to it costs nothing and can point at an instance you run yourself.
Write down what you change and why — your future self will thank you.

sections.heading: Bluesky At Protocol
paragraphs: The short version: Bluesky runs on the open AT Protocol, whose public API is free — an account plus an app password is all a bot needs to post.

So what does that look like when you're actually doing it? createSession returns an access token, and app.bsky.feed.post publishes a post. No middleman, no paid 'basic tier' for your own account's posting, and the protocol is openly specified so the implementation is boring in the best way.
